response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Fabricator files are swapped/clobbered, deleting category fabricators

Affected:
- spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1-4
- spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:1-27

Explanation:
category_fabricator.rb now defines `:embeddable_host`, while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category). This looks like a botched rename, and the names no longer match the contents. It makes the fabricators hard to find and easy to break. If the files are loaded or removed independently, the fabricators go missing. Swap the contents back.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
# category_fabricator.rb: restore the category fabricators
# embeddable_host_fabricator.rb: Fabricator(:embeddable_host) { host "eviltrout.com"; category }
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Host matching is case-sensitive and ignores stored scheme/port; the spec uses unnormalized hosts

Affected:
- app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-18

Explanation:
The query compares `lower(host)` to the URI host, which is not downcased. URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer such as `Example.com` fails to match. The stored host can also include a port (the validation allows `:8080`), but `uri.host` omits the port, so those hosts never match.

`before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!`, which raises NoMethodError when host is nil. It also mutates the attribute in place, so dirty tracking may miss the change.

The embed_controller spec fabricates `host: 'http://discourse.org'`. This relies on the normalization, and the `/1234` path is stripped.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
before_validation do
  self.host = host.to_s.sub(/\Ahttps?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*\z/, '')
end
where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).first
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Admin controller crashes on missing records or params

Affected:
- app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-32

Explanation:
`update` and `destroy` call `.first` and then use the result without a nil check, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises if the key is absent. Use `find`, or return 404, and use strong params or `require`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
host = EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Migration fails or breaks when settings are missing, and is open to SQL injection

Affected:
- db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-25

Explanation:
`execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError on a nil row when no `embed_category` setting exists, which is the common case. The same applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup, since that row may not exist if the default was never saved. Host values are interpolated into the SQL unescaped, so a quote breaks the migration. Hosts with a scheme or path are inserted without normalization. Also, `change` with raw `execute` and DELETE is irreversible.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
row = execute(...).first
category_id = row ? row['id'].to_i : 0
# fall back to the Category with id SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id
# use ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h.strip) for each host
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: TopicEmbed passes a category id as `category` and ignores a nil category

Affected:
- app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-43

Explanation:
`PostCreator` receives `category: eh.try(:category_id)`. `record_for_host` returns false when the URL is invalid, and `false.try` is fine. When there is no match, the category is nil and the topic falls back to the default instead of the old setting. Verify that PostCreator accepts an id under `category`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
category: eh.try(:category_id)  # verify PostCreator accepts ids, or use the category name
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Client-side issues in the host editor and store

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-200
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22

Explanation:
`saveChanges` performs a PUT that does nothing; the server `update` just re-renders. In the store, `obj[k].map` assumes an array, and `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array. Unresolved ids become undefined entries. `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
type.replace(/_/g, '-')
~~~
